title: FAVIS: Fast and Versatile protocol for metabarcoding of bulk Insect Samples
author: Elżbieta waszkiewicz-Eggebrecht
materials: Move all insect bottles to the weighing station.

DNA purification using King Fisher Flex 96 robot For our project we purify a 225 µL aliquot of lysate from each sample using silica-coated magnetic beads with the KingFisher Cell and Tissue DNA kit on a King Fisher Flex 96 robot (both Thermo Scientific) according to manufacturer instructions. You can use alternative kits in your project but make sure you optimize the amount of lysate input needed to obtain enough DNA for your purposes. If you don't have a King Fisher Flex 96 robot, you can purify your DNA manually (see our proposed alternative DNA purification method in step 17 below) but this will take substantially longer to process.

Follow your kit specific instructions. We recomend eluting the purified DNA with 100 μL of elution buffer or TE buffer. (Note that buffers containing EDTA, such as TE, can inihbit some poIymerases. Qiagen Multiplex polymerase that we recommend in Library Preparation steps works well with TE but if you plan to experiment with different polymerases, then you're safer using purified water to elute DNA).
Wait 5 min until dry (on magnetic stand).

steps.title: Set up washing stations
steps.instruction: Place two 80 L plastic containers on the bench: one filled with 10 % bleach solution (mix 9 parts water with 1 part laboratory bleach, NaOCl 47‑50 %) and a second with soap‑and‑water solution. Metal items may be left in bleach for no more than 10 min; all equipment must stay at least 15 min in bleach, then be transferred to the soap‑and‑water container for rinsing. Empty both containers weekly.

steps.title: Create numbered working stations
steps.instruction: Divide the bench into 41 stations, each 30 cm wide, and number them 1‑41.

steps.title: Disinfect benches with bleach
steps.instruction: Using a squirt bottle filled with 10 % bleach solution and a paper towel, wipe the entire surface of each working station.

steps.title: Prepare station supplies
steps.instruction: At every station place: one tray, one 500 mL wide‑mouth ethanol bottle, one funnel (to sit on the ethanol bottle), one bottle seal, two Ø7 cm nylon mesh circles (one for ethanol decanting, one for lysate decanting), and one set of large forceps (200 mm).

steps.title: Place insect bottles and label
steps.instruction: Put one insect collection bottle in stations 1‑40. In station 41 place an empty 500 mL Nalgene HDPE bottle as the blank sample and label it B‑DDMMYY (day, month, year). Using a marker, label each sample bottle and its lid with the corresponding station number (1‑41).

steps.title: Optional: Set up spike‑in stations
steps.instruction: Reserve a clean bench; at each spike‑in station place a petri dish and a dedicated pair of forceps. Retrieve each spike‑in species from the freezer and place a small amount into its petri dish with the dedicated forceps.

steps.title: Set up lysis buffer & proteinase K station
steps.instruction: Reserve a clean bench and arrange graduated cylinders (50‑500 mL), small funnels, pipettes and filtered tips. Note that each sample will receive 30‑400 mL of lysis buffer and 30‑400 µL of proteinase K, volume depending on insect biomass (see Table 2).

steps.title: Set up weighing station
steps.instruction: Reserve a clean bench with a precision balance, five coloured stickers (one per biomass category, Table 1), and a laptop for data entry. Record the average weight of an empty bottle, its mesh and any labels beforehand; this will be subtracted from each measured weight to obtain insect biomass (step 8.3).

steps.title: Preheat lysis buffer
steps.instruction: Place the lysis‑buffer bottles in a shaking incubator (e.g., INCU‑Line ILS6, VWR) set to 65‑70 °C and 90 rpm. Invert each bottle once per hour to aid salt dissolution, especially on cold days.

steps.title: Retrieve archive label and rinse specimens
steps.instruction: At station 1, open the insect bottle, remove the archive paper label with large forceps, and if specimens cling to the label, spray 95 % ethanol with a squirt bottle to rinse them back into the bottle.

steps.title: Secure mesh over bottle opening
steps.instruction: Place one Ø7 cm nylon mesh circle over the bottle opening and fasten it with the bottle seal, using the large forceps for assistance.

steps.title: Transfer preservative ethanol to receiving bottle
steps.instruction: Slowly pour the preservative ethanol from the insect bottle through the funnel into the 500 mL ethanol‑receiving bottle, rotating the insect bottle as needed to aid drainage.

steps.title: Drain ethanol for 35 min
steps.instruction: Turn the insect bottle upside down in the funnel and let it rest. Start a 35‑minute timer after the first sample; this duration ensures most ethanol is removed for accurate wet‑weight biomass measurement.

steps.title: Remove mesh, close bottle
steps.instruction: After the timer expires, lift the bottle from the funnel, use forceps to remove the seal and push the mesh to the bottle bottom, then reseal the bottle with its original cap.

steps.title: Clean funnels and equipment
steps.instruction: Move each funnel to the 10 % bleach container for at least 15 min, then transfer it to the soap‑and‑water container for rinsing. Repeat for all stations.

steps.title: Weigh insect bottles and record
steps.instruction: Place each insect bottle (still containing the mesh) on the precision balance, record the absolute weight in the spreadsheet, and note the station number.

steps.title: Calculate insect biomass and colour‑code
steps.instruction: Subtract the pre‑measured weight of an empty bottle + mesh + labels from the absolute weight to obtain insect biomass. Use an Excel formula to automate the calculation and apply conditional formatting to colour‑code each sample according to its biomass category (Table 1).

steps.title: Sort bottles into biomass categories
steps.instruction: Attach a coloured tag (per Table 1) to the top of each insect bottle according to its calculated biomass category.

steps.title: Add optional biological spike‑ins
steps.instruction: Working one bottle at a time (excluding the blank), open the cap and add the following specimens: Drosophila serrata – 1, D. jambulina – 1, D. bicornuta – 3, Shelfordella lateralis – 2, Gryllodes sigillatus – 1, Gryllus bimaculatus – 1. Reseal the bottle and move it to the lysis station.

steps.title: Add lysis buffer to each bottle
steps.instruction: Using a graduated cylinder and a small funnel, add the sample‑specific volume of pre‑heated lysis buffer (30‑400 mL, per Table 2) to the insect bottle. Pour slowly to minimise foaming and rinse the bottle walls so that any insects adhering to the glass fall into the buffer.

steps.title: Add proteinase K to each bottle
steps.instruction: Add the sample‑specific amount of proteinase K (30‑400 µL, per Table 2) to the lysis buffer in the bottle. For speed, you may first mix proteinase K into the bulk lysis buffer before dispensing.

steps.title: Close bottles and pre‑mix buffer
steps.instruction: Seal each insect bottle with its cap. If you pre‑mixed proteinase K into the bulk buffer, simply add the calculated volume of “lysis buffer + proteinase K” to each bottle (see Table 12).

steps.title: Preheat insect bottles in water bath
steps.instruction: Place the sealed bottles in a water bath circulating at 60 °C. Small volumes (30‑100 mL) require 30 min; large volumes (200‑400 mL) require 40 min to reach 56 °C before incubation.

steps.title: Incubate samples at 56 °C
steps.instruction: Transfer the pre‑heated bottles to a shaking dry incubator set to 56 °C and 90 rpm. Incubate for 2 h 45 min.

steps.title: Optional: Measure ethanol concentration
steps.instruction: While samples incubate, pour ~5 mL of ethanol from each receiving bottle into a 10 mL beaker, measure density with a density meter, and record. If the concentration is <90 %, add 95 % ethanol to the receiving bottle and repeat measurement until >90 % is achieved.

steps.title: Wipe stations with bleach after incubation
steps.instruction: After incubation, spray all working‑station surfaces with 10 % bleach solution and wipe with a paper towel.

steps.title: Set up lysate collection containers
steps.instruction: At each station place a labelled 250 mL Nalgene HDPE lysate‑collecting bottle and a labelled 2 mL screw‑cap microtube. Use a 500 mL bottle only if the final lysate volume exceeds 200 mL.

steps.title: Decant lysate into labelled bottles
steps.instruction: Remove each insect bottle from the incubator, place a second Ø7 cm mesh over the opening, secure with the seal, and slowly pour the lysate through the funnel into the labelled lysate‑collecting bottle. Allow dripping to stop, then close the lysate bottle.

steps.title: Replace archive label and refill ethanol
steps.instruction: If an archive paper label was removed earlier, re‑insert it into the insect bottle. Then pour the ethanol that was decanted in step 7.4 back into the bottle and reseal for long‑term storage.

steps.title: Store trays and tools in bleach then soap
steps.instruction: Place all trays, ethanol‑receiving bottles, bottle seals and forceps into the 10 % bleach container for at least 15 min, then move them to the soap‑and‑water container for rinsing.

steps.title: Aliquot lysate for DNA purification (optional)
steps.instruction: Gather a 1000 µL pipette, a box of filtered 1000 µL tips and a 96‑well microtube rack. Gently shake each lysate bottle to homogenise before aliquoting.

steps.title: Transfer lysate aliquots to microtubes
steps.instruction: From each lysate bottle dispense two 900 µL aliquots into the corresponding labelled 2 mL microtube (one per tube).

steps.title: Store lysate aliquots at –20 °C
steps.instruction: Keep both the remaining lysate bottles and the microtube aliquots at –20 °C until DNA extraction, unless proceeding immediately.

steps.title: Thaw lysate microtubes before purification
steps.instruction: Remove the 96‑well microtube rack from the freezer and let it thaw at room temperature, or place it in a 37 °C shaking incubator. Ensure all lysate is completely thawed and mixed before the next step.

steps.title: Transfer lysate to deep‑well plate
steps.instruction: Open each microtube and pipette 225 µL of lysate into a 96‑well deep‑well plate (2.2 mL capacity). Add 225 µL ddH₂O to well H9 (negative control) and 225 µL of a lysate with known DNA concentration to well H10 (positive control). Leave wells H11 and H12 empty for later library‑prep controls.

steps.title: Add magnetic bead solution to plate
steps.instruction: Prepare fresh 80 % ethanol aliquots. Add 585 µL of magnetic‑bead solution to each well of the deep‑well plate (except H11 and H12). Using a 100 mL reagent reservoir and an 8‑ or 12‑channel pipette can speed this step.

steps.title: Add lysate and controls to plate
steps.instruction: To each well (except H11/H12) add 390 µL of the corresponding lysate (or control) and mix by pipetting up‑and‑down. Note: bead‑to‑lysate ratio is 1.5‑2.0×; total volume per well must not exceed 1000 µL.

steps.title: Incubate and wash beads with ethanol
steps.instruction: Incubate the plate 5 min at room temperature, then place on a magnetic stand for 5 min. Remove supernatant with a multichannel pipette. Add 975 µL of 80 % ethanol to each well, incubate 1 min on the magnetic stand, and discard supernatant. Repeat the ethanol‑wash step once more.

steps.title: Elute DNA with TE buffer
steps.instruction: Remove the plate from the magnetic stand and add 100 µL of TE × 1 (or nuclease‑free water) to each well. Mix, place back on the magnetic stand for 2 min, then transfer 40 µL of the eluate to a new 96‑well plate for long‑term storage and the remaining 40 µL to a second plate for working DNA stock.

steps.title: Prepare PCR1 master mix
steps.instruction: For a 96‑well plate (95 samples + 1 negative control) prepare the following master mix (multiply by 95): 4 µL 10 µM COI BF3 primer mix, 4 µL 10 µM COI BR2 primer mix, 28 µL ddH₂O, and 4 µL DNA template per well (total 40 µL). Include one well with ddH₂O only as the PCR 1 negative control.

steps.title: Run PCR1 and verify on gel
steps.instruction: Perform PCR 1 in a pre‑PCR room using the appropriate cycling program (not detailed here). Load 2 µL of each PCR product with 2 µL loading dye onto a 2.5 % agarose gel and run to confirm amplification.

steps.title: Clean up PCR1 products with beads
steps.instruction: Prepare fresh 80 % ethanol. Transfer 20 µL PCR1 product to a 96‑well deep‑well plate, add 40 µL magnetic‑bead solution (2× volume), mix, and incubate 5 min at room temperature. Place on magnetic stand 2 min, discard supernatant, wash twice with 150 µL 80 % ethanol (1 min each), air‑dry beads 5 min, add 20.5 µL TE buffer, mix, stand 2 min, transfer 20 µL eluate to a new 96‑well plate, and store at 4 °C (short term) or –20 °C (long term).

steps.title: Prepare index primer solutions
steps.instruction: Dilute i5 and i7 index primers to 10 µM in TE buffer, preparing separate solutions for each index.

steps.title: Prepare PCR2 master mix
steps.instruction: For a 96‑well plate (95 samples + 1 negative control) prepare the following master mix (multiply by 100): 5 µL 2× Qiagen Multiplex PCR Master Mix, 0.5 µL 10 µM i5 index, 0.5 µL 10 µM i7 index, 2 µL ddH₂O, and 1 µL cleaned PCR1 product per well (total 9 µL; add 1 µL water to reach 10 µL). Include one well with ddH₂O only as the PCR 2 negative control.

steps.title: Run PCR2 with cycling conditions
steps.instruction: In a post‑PCR room run PCR 2 (10 µL) with the following program: initial denaturation 95 °C 30 s; 6‑7 cycles of denaturation 94 °C 30 s, annealing 50 °C 30 s, extension 72 °C 30 s; final extension 72 °C 60 s; hold at 4 °C.

steps.title: Run PCR2 products on gel
steps.instruction: Load 2 µL of each PCR 2 product with 2 µL loading dye onto a 2.5 % agarose gel and run to verify indexing.

steps.title: Pool libraries based on band intensity
steps.instruction: For each 96‑well plate, combine PCR 2 products into a 1.5 mL microtube according to gel band intensity: 1 µL from a strong band, 2 µL from a medium band, 4 µL from a weak band, and 8 µL from a lane with no visible band.

steps.title: Clean pooled libraries with ProNex beads
steps.instruction: Using the Promega ProNex Size‑Selective Purification System, add 80 µL of pooled library to magnetic beads at a 1:1.5 (v/v) ratio, follow the manufacturer’s protocol, and retain the cleaned pool.

steps.title: Measure pool concentrations on Qubit
steps.instruction: Quantify each cleaned plate pool with a Qubit fluorometer and record the concentration.

steps.title: Create two master pools (A & B)
steps.instruction: Combine four plate pools (total 384 libraries) into Master Pool A and another four plate pools into Master Pool B, adjusting volumes based on the concentrations measured in the previous step.

steps.title: Clean master pools and resuspend
steps.instruction: Clean each Master Pool using ProNex beads at a 1:1.3 (v/v) ratio. After washing, resuspend the final product in TE × 0.1 (or nuclease‑free water) to the desired final concentration.

steps.title: Measure master pool concentrations
steps.instruction: Measure the DNA concentration of Master Pools A and B on a Qubit fluorometer following the manufacturer’s instructions.

steps.title: Quality‑check master pools on Bioanalyzer
steps.instruction: Run each Master Pool on a Bioanalyzer or TapeStation to assess library quality (e.g., absence of primer‑dimers). If primer‑dimers are detected, repeat the bead‑cleaning step (see step 19.5).
